events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Tuesday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas

Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday
at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will

period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp

weather.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and Southeastern Burlington. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Confidence is high on at least moderate tidal flooding occurring with Thursday morning's high tide. Tide levels could potentially reach the major threshold. Stay tuned to the latest forecast for any changes.

location.region: Ocean; Atlantic; Coastal Atlantic; Coastal Ocean; Southeastern Burlington

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along the beaches, Albemarle, Croatan, and Roanoke Sounds, Kitty Hawk Bay, and adjacent tidal creeks. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday morning. * IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Ocean overwash and beach erosion may begin to impact areas adjacent to the ocean starting Wednesday night. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. Initially ocean overwash and bech erosion will be a concern as 8-12 ft seas impact the area beaches. However, as winds switch to a SW direction Thursday afternoon and evening minor water level rises (around 1-2 ft) on soundside locations will be possible as water sloshes back towards the eastern end of the Pamlico Sound.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Largest surf expected on the west side of the islands. * WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to 9 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am.

of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock
damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of
harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am.

such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9- 8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

However as winds switch to a SW direction Thursday afternoon and evening minor water level rises (around 1-2 ft) on soundside locations of Hatteras and Ocracoke Island will be possible as water sloshes back towards the eastern end of the Pamlico Sound.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...1 1/2 to 2 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern New Haven County. In New York, Bronx, Northwest Suffolk, Northern Queens and Northern Nassau Counties. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon high tides. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 3 to 6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially extending into the Friday afternoon high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, now through 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9- 8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 5000 feet in elevation. Total snow accumulations between 7 and 14 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph. * WHERE...Washington Pass. * WHEN...From 7 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult across Washington Pass. Snowfall rates late Wednesday night into early Thursday morning could approach one inch per hour at times. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures in the upper Methow Valley will be near to just above freezing. Heavier precipitation intensities could drive wet snow down to valley floors at times near Mazama and Winthrop with low confidence for accumulations.

location.region: Western Okanogan County

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 24 at 10:06PM PST until November 27 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Spokane WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 5000 feet in elevation. Total snow
accumulations between 7 and 14 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40
mph.

* WHERE...Washington Pass.

* WHEN...From 7 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult across Washington Pass.
Snowfall rates late Wednesday night into early Thursday morning
could approach one inch per hour at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures in the upper Methow Valley will
be near to just above freezing.  Heavier precipitation intensities
could drive wet snow down to valley floors at times near Mazama and
Winthrop with low confidence for accumulations.
weather.instruction:
For the latest travel information in Washington, go to
https://wsdot.wa.gov/travel

Persons should consider delaying travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas. * WHEN...Through Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce hazardous surf with a high risk of rip currents along east- facing reefs at least through Friday afternoon. Another trade- wind surge is expected starting Thursday, likely continuing the threat of rip currents beyond Friday.

location.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 3:34PM ChST until November 27 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce
hazardous surf with a high risk of rip currents along east-
facing reefs at least through Friday afternoon. Another trade-
wind surge is expected starting Thursday, likely continuing
the threat of rip currents beyond Friday.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Washington... Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County. .Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate flood. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch. * WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening. * IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet. - Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage possible. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:30AM PST until November 27 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are
likely, with exceeding flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 530 PM PST.
weather.areaDesc: Mason, WA

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Largest surf expected on the west side of the islands. * WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.0-8.2 feet will likely peak between 8 AM and 11 AM.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 2:55AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 1 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...Northeast Suffolk County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 4 PM EST Friday. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 4 to 8 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning, and if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly. Similarly if strongest winds linger later into the evening, the Thursday evening water level forecast could be a few tenths higher.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches

flood stage possible.

weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM PST.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the following rivers in Washington... Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County. .Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage this morning. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch. * WHEN...Until Friday morning. * IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including SR 106, and much of the farm land. Flooding will occur all along the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams within and near the Skokomish River Basin. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet. - Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage possible. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8 feet on 03/19/1997. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Mason, WA

the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1245 PM PST.

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and rough
surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern

Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST this
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

weather.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.5 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. F For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft expected. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 11:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 11:30 AM PST Thursday was 18.0 feet. - Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage just after midnight tonight to 15.7 feet late tomorrow evening. It will then rise to 15.8 feet early Saturday morning. It will fall to 14.4 feet Sunday afternoon. It will then rise to 15.7 feet late Monday evening. It will fall again and remain below flood stage. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8 feet on 03/19/1997. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From Wednesday, November 25 to Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM PST Thursday was 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight to 15.7 feet late tomorrow evening. It will then
rise to 15.8 feet early Saturday morning. It will fall to 14.4
feet Sunday afternoon. It will then rise to 15.7 feet late Monday
evening. It will fall again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.

deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.description: ...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI...AND NORTH FACING SHORES OF MAUI AND THE BIG ISLAND... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR WEST FACING SHORES OF MAUI... ...COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT IN EFFECT FOR ALL HAWAIIAN ISLANDS... .An extra-large north-northwest (330 to 350 degree) swell will peak well above warning levels this morning. Additionally, higher than predicted water levels could lead to flooding of beaches that typically remain dry, particularly during the pre-dawn high tides this morning. * WHAT...For north-facing shores, surf heights 35 to 45 ft this morning, subsiding to 25 to 35 ft this afternoon for the smaller islands, and building to 20 to 30 feet this afternoon for the Big Island. For west-facing shores, surf 20 to 30 ft this morning, subsiding to 15 to 20 ft this afternoon. A combination of surf and high water levels could produce nuisance coastal flooding. * WHERE...North and west-facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, and north facing shores of Maui and the Big Island. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 6 AM HST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Statement, until 8 AM HST this morning. * IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous. Flooding of beaches that are normally dry, minor coastal erosion, and saltwater inundation.

events.description: Rain will mix with or changeover to wet snow as temperatures quickly drop into the lower to mid 30s this evening. Snow and rain will diminish in intensity Friday before gradually ending.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Rain will transition to snow this afternoon and evening across the Cumberland Plateau and nearby areas, as well as along the southern portions of the east TN mountains and southwest NC. While minor snowfall accumulations are possible, and may lead to slick roads, the main impact is expected to be due to reduced visibilities. Areas that see these higher snowfall rates can expect visibility reductions of 2 miles or less. This will make travel more difficult and perhaps even treacherous due to busier roads due to Thanksgiving travel. Please plan accordingly if planning to travel in or through these areas. If planning to travel from east TN to middle TN you can expect impacts. Using extra caution is advised, slow down, and allow extra distance between yourself and other vehicles.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 26 at 11:12AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards...beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Light snow showers are expected across the mountains near the Tennessee border and across Macon and northern Jackson counties overnight. By Friday morning, snowfall of 1 to 2 inches, with locally higher amounts is possible across the higher elevations of western Graham and western Macon Counties, as well as the higher elevations of the Smokies. A dusting to up to an inch is possible across the upslope areas of the Northern Mountains. The snow may briefly mix with light freezing rain or drizzle before ending Friday morning. While a brief period of wintry weather is possible in the valleys across the Tennessee border counties Friday morning, little-to-no accumulation is expected in these areas. Motorists planning travel across the high elevations of southwest North Carolina tonight or Friday morning should plan for potential slick spots on roads.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Light rain transitioning to light snow has begun in areas across north Georgia this evening as expected. Temperatures below approximately 2500' remain just at or above freezing, meaning no significant accumulations are expected but snow could briefly linger on elevated or grassy surfaces through the night. Above 2500' temperatures have fallen to at or below freezing. Up to an inch of accumulation could occur in these locations with isolated amounts of around 2" along some of the higher peaks. Overall travel impacts should be minimal. Recent warm temperatures should keep roadways mostly clear, though care should be had on bridges and overpasses, especially in elevated locations. For more information or to report snowfall amounts at your location, please visit www.weather.gov/atlanta.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: We will continue to some light rain or snow in the lower elevations with little or no snow accumulation overnight, but the higher elevations especially above 2500 feet will be primarily snow overnight into Friday morning. While the ground is warm, some of the higher terrain of the Plateau, southwest Virginia, the east Tennessee mountains, and the mountains of southwest North Carolina will see around an inch of snow accumulation. A few mountain peaks may see accumulations in the 2 to 3 inch range. While the ground is still fairly warm this early in the season, be alert for slippery spots on roadways if traveling in these areas, especially on bridges and overpasses. Please plan accordingly if planning to travel in or through these areas. Using extra caution is advised, slow down, and allow extra distance between yourself and other vehicles. |

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 26 at 7:25PM EST until November 27 at 11:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Collier County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, through Friday
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Bayshore locations along San Pablo and San Francisco Bays. * WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Sunday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

dangers of flooding.

or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.
